paragraphs: Clean 2D cross-section drawings — every profile is available in any compound from the specification table below. Dimensional conformity to ISO 3302-1, class E1 to E3 as recorded on the drawing; ±0.2 mm held on critical dimensions, with the tolerance on any one dimension set by the section rather than applied across the profile.

fields.note: 50 words · live is 25 · the first clause is kept because it is the decoupling statement the grommets and bushes tables were missing. The addition is the standard. ±0.2 mm on its own is a number without a frame; naming ISO 3302-1 and its E classes turns it into a claim an engineer can check, and the closing clause is the honest qualifier — a thin wall and a large hollow section cannot hold the same tolerance

fields.label: Cards ×8 + 1
rows: Send your drawing or a sample of the profile you are replacing
fields.note: Eight plus one, unchanged in count and in code. Two caption edits only: Solid Cord gains “and vulcanised joints”, because a jointed cord ring is a distinct product a buyer searches for and Margo makes it; and the Custom card gains “or a sample of the profile you are replacing”, because replacement profiles arrive as worn lengths far more often than as drawings. The eight must not be padded to make a rounder number — each entry implies a tooled die, and a library card for a die that does not exist is a quotation that fails

fields.label: Card CTA
fields.note: New, and this is the one addition worth making to this block. The cards currently do not link anywhere, so a buyer who has identified their section has no next step from the card itself. Passing the code in the query string means the enquiry arrives already identifying the profile — the cheapest possible qualification, and something no competitor page in this category does

notes: The part codes are the retrieval anchors. EXT-DS01 and its siblings are unique strings that appear nowhere else on the internet. A buyer who has one on a drawing or a delivery note searches it verbatim and lands here. Keep them visible, keep them in the ItemList, and never change them once published.

The cross-sections must be SVG with text, not flat images. Eight profile drawings rendered as PNG publish eight pictures and zero words; as inline SVG with a <title> and <desc> per drawing they publish the section name and its function to a crawler as well.
Card titles are <h3>. Eight <h3>s under one <h2> is a clean outline and each is a searched term — rubber P-seal profile, rubber U-channel manufacturer India, EPDM D-section seal.

ISO 3302-1 belongs here and on every other product page. It is the dimensional tolerance standard for moulded and extruded rubber, it costs one clause, and it is the difference between a tolerance claim and a tolerance specification.

The query-string CTA needs the form to read it. If /contact cannot pre-fill from a parameter, the link still works and the parameter still shows in analytics as the profile the buyer was looking at — which is worth having on its own.

sections.title: Manufacturing process
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Finished Profile · four named stages, each accurate · the only process block on the site · the cure methods named are a real capability claim and nothing else on the site mentions them

fields.label: Eyebrow
fields.note: [no change]

fields.label: H2
fields.note: [no change — it names the span of the process in five words and is the best section heading on the site]

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Every extrusion follows four tightly controlled stages. Each is monitored in-process and logged against the batch record, so a length delivered eighteen months from now can be traced back to the mix that made it.
leads: Each is monitored in-process and logged against the batch record
marked: Every extrusion follows four tightly controlled stages. **Each is monitored in-process and logged against the batch record**, so a length delivered eighteen months from now can be traced back to the mix that made it.
fields.note: 36 words · live is 22 · the live sentence is kept and one clause added. Traceability is the claim the batch record implies and never states, and it is what an OEM quality auditor is actually asking about — it also connects directly to the “full batch traceability” badge in section 06, which currently sits on the page unsupported by any explanation

fields.label: Stages ×4
rows: Base polymer blended with fillers, plasticisers and vulcanisation agents to an in-house formulation. Mixed on site, not bought in.
Continuous profile formed through a precision-machined tooling die at controlled barrel temperature.
Vulcanisation by salt bath, microwave tunnel or LCM line — the method selected for the compound and the section.
Water quench, in-line dimensional check, then precision cut to length or spooled to order.
fields.note: Four stages, four stages — no count change and almost no copy change. This block is accurate as written. One clause is added to stage 01 because “in-house formulation” is doing quiet work that deserves to be loud: a compounder and a converter are different businesses, and this is where the page says which one Margo is. Stage 03 is left alone — naming salt bath, microwave tunnel and LCM is a real and specific capability claim that appears on no other page of this site

notes: Three cure methods named is the most technically credible sentence on this website. Salt bath (LCM), microwave and hot-air tunnel curing are the three continuous vulcanisation routes for extruded rubber, and a supplier that names which ones it runs is telling an engineer it owns the line rather than subcontracts it. It should be repeated on /about, where the manufacturing capability list currently mentions none of them.
Stage headings are <h3>, numbered in a <li> or <dl>, not four loose <div>s. The order is the meaning here.
Do not mark this up as HowTo. It describes what Margo does, not what the reader does. The HowTo node belongs on section 05, which is genuinely a procedure the reader follows.

“rubber extrusion process” and “continuous vulcanisation” are informational searches with high volume and low commercial competition. This block can rank for them, and a buyer who arrives on an explainer and finds a manufacturer is a better outcome than one who arrives on a product page.

Parameter 04 is the one to protect: naming ASTM D395 Method B and asking the buyer for their pass criterion is a level of technical conversation no competitor page in this category opens, and it is the same standard the leak-test sheet leans on. Margo runs it in-house

fields.label: Closing line
fields.value: Have all four? Send them with your section drawing. [ Request a Quote → ] /contact
fields.note: New. The block explains what to send and then stops. A four-step guide with no step five leaves the reader having done the thinking and given no way to act on it — and this is the highest-intent moment on the page, because a buyer who has just assembled four parameters is ready to send them

notes: This is the only block on the site that earns a HowTo node. Four ordered steps, a defined outcome, a stated turnaround. HowTo with four HowToStep children, each carrying the parameter name and its body text verbatim.

“How do I specify a rubber extrusion profile?” is answered here and almost nowhere else on the internet by a manufacturer. It is a question an engineer asks once per project and the answer is worth citing, which is exactly the shape of query a generative engine returns a source for.
Heading levels. <h2> for the section, <h3> for each of the four parameters. The numbers are presentational and belong in CSS, not in the heading text.
The 48-hour figure is the site constant and must render from the same source as the eleven other places it appears.

Repeat this block’s pattern on the moulded categories. Every category page would benefit from a “specify in four lines” equivalent, and none of the other ten has one. It is the strongest structural idea on this website and it exists on one page.

The documentation package is the citable passage. Four named documents supplied as standard is unusual in this category and it is checkable. It belongs on /certifications and /export as well, where it appears nowhere.
Markup. The quote is <blockquote> with <cite>; the two test groups are <h3> plus <ul>. Standards go in <code> or a monospace span so they are visually separable from the test names.
